title: Budget night with Theo
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Alex and their brother Theo go through Alex's budget after the studio raised its offer, how Alex negotiated extra vacation days and a training budget, and the coast trip costs, while Theo's question about a retirement account is deferred and never picked up.

utterances.text: Okay, show me this famous spreadsheet.
It's not famous. It's three columns and a lot of yellow.
Yellow means what?
Don't know yet. So, the new salary. After my counter, the studio raised the offer by four thousand. Still a bit less than the insurance job, but way better than their first number.
Wait, so you took a pay cut on purpose?
A small one, for work I actually like. I did the math. It's about three hundred a month.
And where does three hundred a month come from?
Mostly takeout. I spent a ridiculous amount on dinners after bad days at the old job.
Sad burrito money.
Exactly. No more sad burritos. And I'm cooking more anyway, because of the running.
Okay, responsible. Did you get anything besides the four thousand?
That's the part I'm proud of. I asked about other stuff. Five extra vacation days, and a training budget. Fifteen hundred a year for courses.
How did you even ask for that? You hate asking for things.
My mentor gave me a negotiation book. Never Split the Difference. The author was an FBI hostage negotiator.
For a design job?
That's what I said! But there's a trick where instead of arguing, you ask an open question. So when they said the base was final, I said, okay, how can we make this work for both of us?
And they just offered stuff?
They did! The hiring manager brought up vacation first. Then I asked for the training budget and a review at six months. Yes to all three.
Huh. I need that book for my review in March. Okay, what about the trip with Sam? Is that yellow?
Green, actually. Six hundred each, max. Gas, food, campgrounds and one motel night.
Six hundred for six days? How?
We camp and cook almost every night. The motel is the splurge.
You're still taking my big tent, right?
If you'll lend it. Sam's tent is technically for two, realistically for one and a half.
It's in the garage. Bring it back dry this time.
That was one time!
Oh, and remind me to ask about your retirement account thing, the rollover from the old job. Later, though.
Sure, later. Okay, last yellow cell. The flight home for Mom's birthday.
I'll split it with you. Book it this week before prices jump.
Deal. Look at us, being adults.
